title: Cascode current mirror
description: A K:1 cascode current mirror. Four unit devices: the bottom reference (diode-connected), the reference-branch cascode (diode-connected, stacked on it), the output mirror device, and the output cascode. The cascode devices force the two mirror devices to sit at the SAME low drain voltage, so the channel-length-modulation ($\lambda$) mismatch between them is essentially zero and the systematic ratio error collapses. That matched bias is the whole point of cascoding a mirror: unlike the simple mirror, the output current no longer drifts with the output node voltage. The cost is output compliance: the output node must clear two stacked saturation voltages before the cascode leaves saturation, so $V_{out}$ cannot swing as low as a simple mirror's. Both mirror devices bind width-first as unit-device multiples (output width = K times the reference). The two reference devices are diode-connected, so their drops are read off the table rather than estimated, and the output devices are biased from what the reference actually sits at. Random matching is the Pelgrom spread of the bottom mirror pair; the cascodes only pass the current and so do not set the ratio.

params.name: VDD
params.note: supply; the reference diode stack must fit under it

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the mirror serves; a cascode mirror needs it high enough to clear two stacked saturation voltages

params.name: L
params.note: mirror-device length: longer L lowers lambda and adds matching area

params.name: gm_id_m
params.note: mirror inversion: lower gm/ID (higher V*) tightens current matching but costs compliance headroom

params.name: v_margin
params.note: extra output headroom budgeted above the two-saturation-voltage floor

doc.title: Reference mirror device (bottom, diode)
doc.description: The bottom reference device, diode-connected at the input current. Its drain sits at the mirror node voltage; that same voltage is imposed on the output mirror device by the cascode stack, so the two share a matched vds. Exposes its width for the output side to scale from.

doc.title: Reference-branch cascode (diode)
doc.description: The diode-connected cascode stacked on the reference device, carrying the same reference current. Its source stands on the mirror node rather than the bulk, so its body bias is declared as that node's voltage - the reference diode's own drop - rather than defaulted to zero, which would understate its threshold. Its vgs adds to the bottom device's to set the reference stack's top rail; the output cascode scales from its width.

params.name: vsb_rc
params.note: the source sits on the mirror node, not the bulk

doc.title: Output cascode
doc.description: The output-branch cascode: a K-times-wider copy of the reference cascode, sized width-first. Its source stands on the same mirror node, so it carries the same declared body bias. It passes the output current and holds the output mirror device at the matched low drain voltage. Its saturation voltage sets the second term of the output compliance floor.

params.name: vds_oc
params.note: output node minus the mirror node

params.name: vsb_oc
params.note: the source sits on the mirror node, not the bulk

rows.name: sys_err
rows.note: lambda mismatch between the two mirror devices; near zero because the cascode holds them at the same vds

rows.name: v_in_ref
rows.note: the reference diode stack's top rail (two stacked vgs)

rows.name: sigma_ratio
rows.note: random 1-sigma error of the K:1 ratio from the bottom mirror pair; the K-times-larger output device contributes 1/sqrt(K) of the reference spread

rules.note: output floor: the output mirror and the output cascode each need one saturation voltage, plus a design margin (two stacked vdsat)
matched-vds cascoding drives the lambda error to nearly zero
the two stacked diode drops of the reference branch must fit under the supply
